claim: cap_limits() turns any unreadable or unparsable cap.json into a hard StoreError::Corrupt, and envelope_for now propagates it with `?`. Under the threat model local data is untrusted, and here is how it happens: the owner hand-edits cap.json, say to `"work": 0` to stop all runs (NonZeroUsize rejects 0), or drops `source`. From then on (a) every keepalive on a hold with a classed item fails after its ticks are saved and before delivery is committed (keepalive.rs:761), so the orchestrator's keepalive loop breaks; (b) cancel saves the cancellation, then returns Err from envelope_for (engine.rs:431), so cold puts a hold that really is cancelled into `errors`, leaves it out of `cancelled`, and exits 1; (c) `cap set` without `--review` reads the bad file (cap.rs:102) and fails, so only `cap reset` recovers, and the "store corrupt: <path>: ..." message names neither cap.json's purpose nor `vigil cap reset`. Admission (hold add or create with --cap) failing closed is fine. The display path and the owner's own set command should not fail.
suggested_fix: in envelope_for, fall back to default limits when cap.json cannot be read, or omit `cap` and add a persist-style warning. In cap_set, treat an unreadable file as defaults for the review fallback. Make the Corrupt error for cap.json say "run `vigil cap reset`". One lib test: write `{"work":0}` to cap.json and assert that keepalive and cancel on a classed hold still return Ok.

claim: `vigil hold --for none --until-idle --cap work` also classes the synthetic idle:<cwd> item as a work run. At the default limit of 1 the creation is refused ("2 working Claude runs ... none, idle:/..."), although idle is never a Claude run. The spec's "count every initial item" allows this, but an orchestrator that combines the two flags gets a confusing refusal.
suggested_fix: leave the idle item unclassed, or refuse `--cap` together with `--until-idle` with a clear error.

claim: When `cap set` omits --review, it keeps the effective review limit but stamps it with the new --until. A review raise that was due to last until tomorrow then expires with a short work raise.

claim: NO-HOLD treats every owner message as a turn end. An owner message typed mid-turn is queued and delivered right after a tool_result, so the turn had not ended. Repro: fauxx c09158c0:817 is an assistant message with stop_reason tool_use (an Agent launch). Its tool_result is at 824 and the queued owner message ("Also do some research...") at 827, enqueued at 822. The checker reports "turn ended ... no hold" at 817. In the 3-day sweep, 18 of the 128 NO-HOLD findings have this shape (owner message directly after a tool_result). One of them is a "[Request interrupted by user]" (6b454199:527), which is_owner_message also counts as an owner message. Two of the report's three NO-HOLD examples are such false findings: fauxx 817, and 6b454199:441 (owner at 456 after a tool_result). This happens whenever the owner types while the agent works.
suggested_fix: judge an owner message as a turn end only when the last user/assistant record before it is an assistant message with no tool_use. Skip "[Request interrupted" messages. Add a test where an owner message follows a tool_result, then rerun the sweep and fix the report's counts and examples.

claim: Once a `vigil hold` is seen, the checker treats it as live until a `vigil cold`, and that silences NO-HOLD for the rest of the file. vigil ends holds in other ways: `vigil cancel <id>`, `mcp__vigil__watch_cancel`, `--deadline-s`/`deadline_s` expiry, and automatic release when every item has ended (main.rs Hold doc). That last case is the pattern SKILL.md §10 prescribes ("each delegated run is an item"). Repro: fauxx c09158c0:9105 runs `vigil hold --id fauxx-hold-3 --deadline-s 3000`. Turn ends at 9122, 9517, 9546 and 9590 have launches unfinished and no keepalive running, and none is flagged. 4040da30:11949 runs `vigil cancel hold-phoe-orch-1`, which the checker never sees. Across the sweep, 8 turn ends pass only because an old hold was never `cold`ed. This happens in every session that uses holds with items or deadlines. These are the breaks §10 targets ("if it releases, make a new hold in the same turn").
suggested_fix: count `vigil cancel` and `watch_cancel` as cold, and expire a hold at its deadline using the records' timestamps. Either count a hold only while a background keepalive on it runs (a keepalive returns when its hold releases), or state the remaining gap in the docstring. Add one test with a deadline or cancel.

claim: Several rules lost their trigger in the router. (a) The roles.md row (40), and to a lesser degree phases.md (39), lists topics where every other row gives a time to read it. B1 (who writes the round-N fixes, `--author`), C3 (briefs say no unslop) and switch-by-budget (Claude low means Sol implements) were in SKILL.md and are now only in roles.md, which no step says to open. (b) The budget.md row dropped "on budget advice", the trigger for B5, and the reviewers.md row dropped "before re-scoping a PR after review". (c) The after-compaction block rereads only SKILL.md, so the phases.md and roles.md rules for the current step are no longer reread, though the old SKILL.md held them. Repro: the orchestrator compacts during review round 2 and rereads SKILL.md as told, then briefs the round-2 fix implementer. B1 and C3 are not in what it reread, and no row sends it to roles.md at a fix round. This happens on every compaction in a long loop.
suggested_fix: change the roles.md row to "At the start (role statement), before every implementer brief or fix round, on budget advice or a reset". Change the phases.md row to "Before §3, before launching red, before green". Restore the two dropped triggers. After the REREAD line (which the hook test pins, so leave it as is), add one sentence: "then reread the reference for the step you are on".

claim: the hold id is read only from `--id` or a `"watch_id":"..."` in the result. A command that pipes the hold JSON through `python3 -c ...["watch_id"]` prints the bare id, so the Hold keeps watch_id None and a later `vigil cancel <id>` never retires it, and the hold stays live until its deadline. Repro: 35442c72:1250 (deadline 14400 s), cancelled at 1333; also 1622 (four holds in a loop, one Hold recorded). A non-numeric `--deadline-s $4` (35442c72:1101 `mk()`) gives deadline None, so the hold never expires instead of taking the 7-day default. A patched run that falls back to the first `w-<hex>-<hex>-<n>` id in the result changes no finding in the sweep.
final_evidence: same class or spot as S2
suggested_fix: fall back to that id match; treat a non-digit deadline as 604800.

claim: A background `vigil wait <id>` is not read as a wait, so a held session is reported as NO-HOLD. Round 1 stashed this as a nit without counting it; it is most of the count. Repro: rerun the report's own sweep command at HEAD: NO-HOLD 39. With KEEPALIVE_RE also accepting `vigil wait`: NO-HOLD 9 (30 gone: c09158c0 16 of 17, 262194c7 8, 83c0b61c 5, 35442c72 1) and MANUAL-TICK 74. The three largest sessions ran `vigil wait` in the background 132 times (c09158c0 51, 262194c7 49, 83c0b61c 32). The report's first NO-HOLD example is one of the false ones: at 83c0b61c:3111 a background `vigil create ...; vigil wait` from line 3057 (timeout 3,300,000 ms) was running and returned at 3163. Same at c09158c0:6674 (`vigil wait fauxx-heartbeat-17` from 6630, returned 6756) and 262194c7:5174 (`vigil wait hold-boss4-p2` from 5087, returned 5228). Anyone who reruns the sweep over these days gets this, every time.
suggested_fix: KEEPALIVE_RE matches `vigil\s+(?:keepalive|wait)\b`; one test with a background `vigil wait <id>` across a turn end; rerun and replace the report's counts and the 83c0b61c example.

claim: Two things count as holding the session after they have stopped doing so. (a) Line 418: a live hold passes a turn end with no background wait running. Tier 1 settled S2 by modelling when a hold dies and kept the premise that a hold alone holds the session. That premise is wrong: a hold is state inside vigil, and only the background keepalive's completion wakes the session (vigil SKILL.md: "ONE hold and one background keepalive call on it running at all times"). §10 now prescribes one bare session hold that lives 7 days, so from now on NO-HOLD cannot fire in any session that made its hold once. Repro (run on a synthetic transcript): `vigil hold`, a background Agent, a background `vigil keepalive w-1 --orchestrator` whose completion notice arrives, then a text reply and an owner message: no finding. That is the "on each return, act and start the next" lapse, and it will be the shape of every lapse once agents follow §10. Round 2 called fauxx 9117/9122 "correct" because fauxx-hold-3 was live; it is correct only because `vigil wait fauxx-hold-3` (line 9109) was running. With S11 fixed, dropping the hold-alone pass changes no finding in the sweep. (b) Line 421, new in 49cbb769: a tick with no completion record counts as running for the rest of the file. Repro: 4040da30 has three such ticks (lines 1705, 2435, 9791; 3 of 65). 4040da30:12837, which round 2 cited as correctly flagged NO-HOLD, is now MANUAL-TICK, credited to a `sleep 270` started 54 hours earlier. After the first lost tick a file can never report NO-HOLD again.
suggested_fix: (a) line 419 becomes `if running: continue`, or report hold-without-wait as its own rule; correct docstring lines 16-19; add the test above. (b) keep N from TICK_RE and count a tick only while the turn end is within N + 60 s of its start (or a timestamp is missing); add a test with timestamps.

claim: The sub-agent exemption added in 49cbb769 knows one of the two kinds of sub-agent, and covers one of the two call forms. Harness sub-agent logs (`*/subagents/*.jsonl`, every record `isSidechain: true`, 602 of 602 checked) do not start with "Act as the ... sub-agent", so each MCP keepalive in them is flagged. Repro: rerun the report's "separately swept" set (118 files): FG-KEEPALIVE 152, where the report says 0 and says the rule does not apply to sub-agents. Second instance: a foreground Bash `vigil keepalive` in a delegated child is still flagged (line 243 has no child check), though SKILL.md §10 says "Only subagents call it in the foreground"; 0 in the sweep, reproduced on a synthetic child. Child detection itself is right: all 80 delegate sessions in the sweep match CHILD_RE and no main session does.
suggested_fix: note when any record has `isSidechain` true; return empty `fg` and `mcp_fg` when the session is a child or a sidechain; two tests.

claim: scout-modules/agent-integration/bin/cap-guard:53-59, scout-modules/agent-integration/skills/build-loop/scripts/transcript-check:319 [pre-existing] The guard inherits transcript-check's async test, `"Async agent launched" in text`, which searches the whole tool_result text. A foreground Agent whose final report quotes that phrase anywhere is read as async, gets no fg_end, and stays unfinished (end=INF) until the next owner message. Reproduction on a real transcript: I copied this orchestrator session (~/.claude/projects/-home-mini-Documents-repos-phoe-nix/4040da30-...jsonl, 35 MB) up to the tool_use of this very review launch (line 17889) and ran the hook with that launch's tool_use_id. It printed "cap-guard: 1 Claude reviewer(s) unfinished (cap 1): 'Opus review W47 router + checker'". That reviewer was a foreground Agent that finished at line 16618. Its toolUseResult says status "completed" with no isAsync, but its report quotes the phrase while discussing transcript-check's own tests. With ~/.config/build-loop/cap-guard-mode set to block, the same input returns permissionDecision "deny". The last owner message was at line 16069, so the reviewer pool stayed poisoned for about 1,800 lines and several rounds. This hits whenever reviewers review transcript-check or cap-guard (the W47/W49 rounds do), and in block mode the agent cannot clear it: "wait for one to finish" never comes true, and on this host the suggested `vigil cap set` does not exist (see nit).
suggested_fix: in transcript-check, decide async from the structured toolUseResult when it is a dict (isAsync true, or status "async_launched"; a dict with status "completed" is foreground). Fall back to the text only when there is no dict, and then match only a leading "Async agent launched". Add a test: a foreground Agent result whose report quotes the phrase must end at its result, for both CAP and cap-guard.

src/v1/jobs.ts:547, src/v1/capture.ts:206, src/v1/import.ts:161 Admission accepts any view.data; component schemas and custom-view lowering are checked only in importCollection; when that fails, finalizeRun throws after writing finalized.json and the importing state; finish has no catch, so every later status/cancel retries, throws and replies INTERNAL; the job never reaches a terminal state and cannot be cancelled (e.g. a TS list view with 65 textColumns vs schema maxItems 64, or a shape field path over 1024 bytes). Fix: run per-view lowering and component-schema checks inside admission (quarantine as a failed capture with a diagnostic); catch import failures in finish and record terminal failed with an import diagnostic.

src/v1/jobs.ts:782, src/v1/jobs.ts:557 cancel calls finish; when another operation holds the lease (a waiting status), finish does nothing, cancel reads running/importing, reports cancelled and writes that stale state outside the lease, possibly regressing a terminal state. Fix: finish-and-record inside withLease; if busy, wait for terminal like S41 or return indeterminate/cancel-too-late; never write state outside the lease.

src/v1/jobs.ts:571, src/v1/jobs.ts:755, src/v1/adapters.ts:338 `cancelRequested || qexJob.state === "killed" && cancelRequested` reduces to cancelRequested; a job that finished on its own before qex cancel is labelled cancelled and cancel replies cancelled instead of cancel-too-late. Fix: cancelled only when cancel was requested and qex reports cancelled/killed (or the job never ran).

src/v1/adapters.ts:127, skills/paneweft-views/SKILL.md:9, src/v1/tools.ts:203, src/cli/v1-commands.ts:28 collect resolves example ids only against the stored catalogue, built only by owner-only `catalogue refresh` with no MCP tool; on a fresh repo an agent following the skill stalls (list_types NOT_FOUND; collect "not declared in the catalogue"). src/v1/jobs.ts:631, src/v1/jobs.ts:898, src/v1/jobs.ts:924 finish never checks that its qexJob is the job of the stage on disk (state.qexId). Cancel holding the export's qexId can, after a waiting status advanced to stage run and submitted the run, finalize the run from the stopped export job (empty staging → terminal failed) while the real run keeps going uncancelled. Also finishExport never re-reads cancel.json, so a cancel written after status read it still submits the run. Fix: under the lease, finish returns without writing when qexJob.id !== state.qexId; finishExport re-reads cancel.json and ends cancelled; when cancel's finishWithin returns non-terminal at stage run, re-read state and cancel the run's qexId (or indeterminate). Red test for the interleaving.
